nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily, titrate to 10 mg once daily as tolerated
medications.purpose: Renin‑angiotensin system blockade to slow CKD progression and improve blood‑pressure control
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 first‑line ACE‑I for CKD with hypertension or proteinuria; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.purpose: Renal‑protective therapy for diabetic kidney disease (eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 first‑line SGLT2‑inhibitor for CKD with eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m² (TA775)

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CV‑risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 first‑line statin for all CKD patients

medications.purpose: Existing antihypertensive (already prescribed) to achieve BP target <130/80 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: Current medication aligns with NICE BP target for CKD

medications.purpose: Treat iron‑deficiency anaemia in CKD (already prescribed)
medications.nice_justification: CKD‑related anaemia management per NICE CKD‑Anaemia guideline

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood‑pressure lowering may cause symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Start ramipril at low dose, monitor BP after each titration step; advise patient to rise slowly

interactions_checked.interaction: Increased risk of hypoglycaemia when combined with insulin
interactions_checked.action: Review insulin dose within 1 week of starting dapagliflozin; consider 10‑20 % reduction in basal and/or bolus doses

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase atorvastatin plasma levels, raising myopathy risk
interactions_checked.action: Use atorvastatin 20 mg (safe dose); if higher dose needed, consider switching to pravastatin or rosuvastatin

contraindications.reason: eGFR 28.7 mL/min/1.73 m² (<30) – risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: Avoid; consider dose reduction only if eGFR ≥30

contraindications.reason: CKD stage 4 – NSAIDs accelerate progression and cause fluid retention
Dual RAAS blockade increases hyperkalaemia and AKI risk; patient not to receive both
contraindications.alternative: Choose either ramipril or losartan (single agent)

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy
contraindications.alternative: Use prophylactic hydration and low‑osmolar contrast if imaging unavoidable

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure reading not provided – assume target not yet achieved; will monitor after ACE‑I initiation
Serum potassium level not available – baseline required before starting ramipril and during titration
Liver function tests (ALT/AST) not available – baseline required before initiating atorvastatin
QRISK score not calculated – CKD considered a CV‑risk equivalent, so statin indicated
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I, statin, or SGLT2‑inhibitor allergies before prescribing
Dietary potassium intake unknown – counsel on low‑potassium diet and monitor serum K+
Smoking status not documented – assess and advise cessation as part of non‑pharmacological plan
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily (titrate to 10 mg) for RAAS blockade, add dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for renal protection, and initiate atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for cardiovascular risk reduction. Continue existing amlodipine and ferrous sulfate. Monitor BP, serum creatinine, eGFR, potassium, glucose, and liver enzymes per NICE NG203. Avoid NSAIDs, metformin, and dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy. Provide lifestyle advice on low‑salt diet, smoking cessation, weight management, and exercise.
